new_statements.relation_note: Orthography follows Indonesian conventions except elongated /aa/, /ii/, /ll/, /oo/ and glottal stop /'/; /j/ described as voiced alveopalatal; accent usually penultimate.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent in Taman usually on the penultimate syllable (me-NYA-rung); at least one lexical item (balien 'shaman') has final stress or stress shared between first and last syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not described (only the remark that in balien stress may be 'shared between the first and the last syllable')
new_statements.exceptions: balien pronounced with final stress or level first+last prominence; 'usually' implies further unlisted exceptions
new_statements.identity_note: Ethnography of the Taman of the upper Kapuas (Kapuas Hulu, West Kalimantan; fieldwork in Taman villages near Putussibau) = tama1335, not the Malayic 'Taman Sesat' of Sekadau; the note explicitly contrasts Taman spelling with Indonesian and lists Taman-specific /aa ii ll oo/ and glottal stop.

readall_conflicts: For the sister dialect Embaloh there is a known disagreement already held by the project under emba1238: Adelaar 1995 states fixed, non-distinctive penultimate stress, whereas Irawan et al. 2024 (Issues in Language Studies 13(1), instrumental study) find fixed final-syllable stress and explicitly say this differs from Adelaar 1995. Whether either finding carries over to Taman is not established by any source.

sources.citation: Abdulmalik, Irmayani; Dedy Ari Asfar; Yusup Irawan; Foni Agus Setiawan; Herpanus; Muhammad Pramulya. 2025 [online June 2026]. Menelusuri variasi bahasa Dayak di Kapuas Hulu: kajian dialektometri atas delapan isolek [Tracing Dayak language variation in Kapuas Hulu: a dialectometric study of eight isolects]. Aksara 37(2): 313-327. doi:10.29255/aksara.v37i2.4920.313-327 (Balai Bahasa / BRIN authors; open access).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. Content: Seguy/Guiter dialectometry over fieldwork vocabulary; comparison tables of five glosses per isolect pair in IPA without stress marks (e.g. Taman Kapuas vs Taman Sibau: bataŋ, padaŋaro, ulu identical; balaŋ ~ balaːŋ 'differ only in vowel length [a] vs [aː], a minor phonological variation'; mintuari vs tu 'person'); Taman Sibau vs Tamambaloh tu ~ tau ('loss of [a] / diphthong [au] in Taman Sibau'), taliŋa vs jame, etc; classification history after Adelaar 1994/2010, Hudson 1970, Smith 2017. The only 'suku kata' mention concerns an Iban/Kantuk gloss.
